text:
All the gold in the world seemed

dissolved into the luminous afternoon!

Barely a rose-colored dusk

tinged the chalice of the trees.


An unforeseen love joined my hand

to yours, dark and trembling.

We were Boaz and Ruth before the lovely

threshing floor that circled the farmhouse!


“Will you love me?” you murmured. Slow and grave,

the gentle promise of the sweet,

loving Moabite trembled on my lips.


And like an “amen” at that instant came

the call to prayer, raised in resonance

by the rhythmic bell of the hermitage.

translation.title: The Promise
translation.editorial_note: The biblical Ruth imagery and the rural Angelus remain central; era is rendered as threshing floor, not epoch.
